propositions: Cloud's three whole-project readers (get_parent_map, get_comment_map, get_issuelinks_map) paginate through opaque nextPageToken cursors at page_size=100 with no test exercising more than one page.

The readers terminate on isLast OR null/absent nextPageToken, but no test asserts the cursor advances across pages, that a second page is fetched and merged, or that a repeated token does not spin forever.
A silent truncation in these readers is invisible because they feed the differ; missing parents/comments/links manifest as incomplete mappings rather than errors.
DC has pagination tests and an AST guard preventing unpaginated whole-project callers; Cloud lacks both, creating asymmetric test parity and allowing a fourth unpaginated reader to be added silently.
A repeated cursor token causes infinite loop when the server returns the same non-null nextPageToken with isLast falsy, and the fail-open exception handler converts this into a silently partial map.

The readers use opaque cursors (not offset arithmetic), so DC's short-page bug cannot occur structurally, but the test suite now has oracles to catch regression and a structural guard to prevent future unpaginated readers.
